rules.quote:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

conditions: An advance payment of at least six months’ rent is permitted if the lease term is six months or longer.
A mutually agreed fee or charge for specified alterations requested by the tenant is not precluded by the cap.
The cap in this subdivision does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

The tenant must have continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months; if additional adult tenants are added before an existing tenant has occupied for 24 months, the statutory alternative occupancy tests apply.
The termination must be based on an applicable at-fault or no-fault just-cause ground listed in the section.

The local-ordinance exclusion applies only in the circumstances specified by the statute, including qualifying ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or qualifying more-protective ordinances adopted or amended later.
For the separately alienable property exception, tenants must have been provided the statutory written exemption notice.

The no-fault grounds include owner/family occupancy, withdrawal from the rental market, specified government or court orders, and demolition or substantial remodel, subject to the statute’s stated requirements and limits.
A tenant’s lease terms and conduct may determine whether an at-fault ground applies; these are not building facts.

When an owner occupies a home and rents to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, but may not make, print, or publish discriminatory statements, notices, or advertisements.
Qualifying housing specifically for seniors may limit occupancy based on age.

building_evidence.limitation: Parcel dwelling count; verify that it describes one building and excludes unrelated structures.

conditions: A tenant in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling may make the Security Deposit Law applicable by sending the landlord a written request and allowing 30 days.

The Act may not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel, motel, or guest-house occupants who are transient or seasonal; or a specified unit held in trust for an immediate family member who is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies it.
Hotel and motel occupants without an alternate residence who reside there continually are covered.
The requirements do not apply to a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee unless the licensee is the landlord of the residential rental property.
The tenant has made efforts to secure or enforce a right under this chapter.
The familial-status prohibition does not apply to housing for older persons as defined in the LAD.
The brochure states a religious-organization exception for preference given to persons of the same religion.

The prohibition applies before a conditional offer; the statute excepts inquiries about a conviction for manufacturing or producing methamphetamine on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex-offender registration.
The ban covers records evaluated either before or after a conditional offer; listed records include expunged, pardoned, vacated/nullified and sealed convictions, and juvenile adjudications.
The statutory exceptions concern methamphetamine manufacture or production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex-offender registration.
